module: Playback of Drive Path Editor paths (splines): associates each vehicle with its linked spline, moves it back to the start, then, once the spline's delay has elapsed, sends the vehicle a vLua command ai.driveUsingPath generated from the spline. Two modes: free (script of nodes x,y,z,r[,v|vl] after Catmull-Rom smoothing and RDP simplification, tolerance 1.0) or navigation graph (wpTargetList and wpSpeeds).
notes: A vehicle is only considered if its spline is linked (isVehicleLink), has the link id (vehicle.linkSplineId), the right linkVehId == vehicle.vid, and isEnabled.
The actual start happens in handlePlayback, called every frame: startPlayback does not start the AI yet.
Free mode: widths are divided by 2 (half-widths); in loop mode (isLoop) the first start node is appended at the end; noOfLaps is only passed for loops.
speedProfileMode: 0 no profile, 1 per-node speeds v, 2 per-node speed limits vl (free mode); in graph mode only mode 1 produces wpSpeeds.
driveInLane is only passed in graph mode (free mode: empty string, with a code comment).
The arguments passed to ai.driveUsingPath include aggression, routeSpeed/routeSpeedMode (if different from off) and avoidCars.

getPlaybackTime.desc: Time elapsed since the start of playback.

startPlayback.desc: Prepares playback: clears the table of ongoing playbacks, adds each vehicle with a linked and enabled spline, moves these vehicles back to their start pose (splineMgr.resetVehiclePose), then resets the time counters to zero.

splines.desc: path splines (fields id, isVehicleLink, linkVehId, isEnabled, delayTime...)

stopPlayback.desc: Sends ai.setState({mode = "stop"}) to each vehicle being played back, moves them back to their start pose, then clears the table and resets the counters to zero.

handlePlayback.desc: To be called every frame: starts the AI of vehicles whose delayTime is reached (only once per vehicle) then advances the playback time.
